rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM music_Track;
rows.note: Assuming "tracks in the catalog" means all rows in music_Track.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS album_count FROM music_Artist ar JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(AlbumId) AS c FROM music_Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assuming "most albums" means the count of rows in music_Album per artist, I'll return only the top artist(s).

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM music_Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY customer_count DESC;
rows.note: Assuming "music store" means the music_Customer table, I'll count customers grouped by Country.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
rows.note: Assuming total invoice revenue means the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS full_name, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS total_spent FROM music_Invoice i JOIN music_Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assuming "amount spent" is the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, using music_Customer names.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount
FROM music_Employee e
JOIN music_Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
HAVING COUNT(c.CustomerId) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM music_Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId
  )
)
rows.note: Assumption: "support rep" refers to music_Customer.SupportRepId linked to music_Employee, and ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM music_PlaylistTrack pt JOIN music_Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge'
rows.note: Assuming the playlist name is exactly 'Grunge' in music_Playlist and counting its rows in music_PlaylistTrack.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM music_Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM music_InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: Assumption: "never purchased" means the track has no row in music_InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM music_Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assuming revenue means the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2012, grouped by BillingCountry.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.Name AS ArtistName
FROM music_Artist ar
JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: Assuming "tracks" link to artists through Track → Album → Artist, and counting distinct genres per artist.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM music_InvoiceLine), 2) AS percentage
FROM music_InvoiceLine il
JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN music_Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY percentage DESC
rows.note: I'll compute revenue per genre from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity) and divide by total revenue across all lines.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM music_Invoice i
JOIN music_InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN music_Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
    SELECT i2.CustomerId
    FROM music_Invoice i2
    JOIN music_InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
    JOIN music_Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
    JOIN music_Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
    WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  );
rows.note: I'll assume "bought" means the track appears in an invoice line, and genre is matched by music_Genre.Name = 'Rock' / 'Jazz'.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM music_Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: invoice revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar month for 2011, and I return the single top month.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM music_Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM music_Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId)
rows.note: Assumption: "employees" refers to music_Employee, and "no customers" means no music_Customer row has SupportRepId equal to their EmployeeId.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date
  FROM music_Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
) AS f
WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01';
rows.note: Assuming "very first purchase" means each customer's earliest invoice date falls in 2010, I'll count those customers.

rows.sql: SELECT al.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds)/60000.0, 1) AS minutes FROM music_Album al JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY al.AlbumId, al.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Milliseconds over each album's tracks, converted to minutes (÷60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, SUM(Total) AS revenue
  FROM music_Invoice
  GROUP BY yr
)
SELECT yr,
       revenue,
       ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr), 1) AS yoy_pct_change
FROM yearly
ORDER BY yr
rows.note: I'll compute yearly revenue from music_Invoice.Total (by invoice year), then the percentage change versus the prior year.

rows.sql: WITH cust AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spend FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_avg FROM cust WHERE spend > (SELECT AVG(spend) FROM cust);
rows.note: I'll treat each customer's spend as the sum of `Total` across their invoices, and the average as the mean of those per-customer totals.

rows.sql:
WITH pa AS (
  SELECT pt.PlaylistId, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS artist_count
  FROM music_PlaylistTrack pt
  JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN music_Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY pt.PlaylistId
)
SELECT p.Name, pa.artist_count
FROM pa
JOIN music_Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pa.PlaylistId
WHERE pa.artist_count = (SELECT MAX(artist_count) FROM pa);
rows.note: Assumption: artists are reached via Track → Album → Artist, and ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM music_InvoiceLine il JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) sub
rows.note: Assuming "invoice contains tracks from more than one genre" means counting distinct GenreId values across its invoice lines' tracks is greater than 1.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS support_rep, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue_2010
FROM music_Invoice i
JOIN music_Customer c ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
JOIN music_Employee e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= '2010-01-01' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2011-01-01'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY revenue_2010 DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll sum invoice totals for 2010 by each customer's support rep, then return the rep with the highest total.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM shop_Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
rows.note: Assuming Discontinued = '1' marks a discontinued product.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM shop_Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany' LIMIT 50
rows.note: Assumption: "based in Germany" means Country = 'Germany' in shop_Suppliers.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM shop_Categories c JOIN shop_Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName HAVING COUNT(p.ProductID) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM shop_Products GROUP BY CategoryID))
rows.note: Assuming "most products" means the count of products in shop_Products per category, I'll return the top category (all tied rows if there's a tie).

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS OrderYear, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM "shop_Orders" GROUP BY OrderYear ORDER BY OrderYear;
rows.note: Assuming "placed" means OrderDate, grouped by the calendar year of OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName AS shipper_name, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS avg_freight FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName
rows.note: Assuming "freight cost" is Freight in shop_Orders, grouped by the shipper linked via ShipVia.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM shop_Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM shop_Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')
rows.note: I'm assuming Andrew Fuller is the row in shop_Employees with FirstName 'Andrew' and LastName 'Fuller', and that "report directly" means ReportsTo points to his EmployeeID.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM shop_Orders o
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2020'
GROUP BY o.EmployeeID
HAVING COUNT(*) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM shop_Orders
    WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2020'
    GROUP BY EmployeeID
  )
);
rows.note: Assuming "handled" means the order's EmployeeID, counting orders with OrderDate in 2020.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM shop_Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM shop_Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the plain average of UnitPrice across all rows in shop_Products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_shipped_to_france FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assuming "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' on shop_Orders, counting all orders regardless of ShippedDate.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), summed per product, ranked descending.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice
FROM shop_Products p
JOIN shop_Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE p.UnitPrice = (
  SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM shop_Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
)
ORDER BY c.CategoryName;
rows.note: Assuming "most expensive" means the highest UnitPrice within each category (ties all included).

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
FROM shop_Orders o
JOIN shop_Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
JOIN "shop_Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'm treating revenue as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over orders dated in 2021, grouped by customer.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM shop_Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: count orders in shop_Orders by OrderDate month for year 2021, returning the top month.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM shop_Orders o
  JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '1998-01-01'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
)
SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, order_count
FROM counts
WHERE order_count = (SELECT MAX(order_count) FROM counts);
rows.note: The shop_Orders table has no orders from 1997. Its OrderDate values run only from 2012 through 2023, so no employee can be credited with 1997 orders.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the julianday difference in days.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM shop_Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0', and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql: SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS order_count FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: count orders by the customer's country (shop_Customers.Country) for orders with OrderDate in 2019.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN shop_Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2023-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2024-01-01'
rows.note: I'll assume revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), using orders dated in 2023, and compare Beverages to all categories.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM shop_Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12) AS t;

WITH order_values AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM shop_Orders o
  JOIN "shop_Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_values
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg);
rows.note: Assumption: order value = sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its lines, averaged per employee across their orders that have lines.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN shop_Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll assume revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from order details, with the order date in 2018 and grouped by the product's supplier.
